payload.generic_root_cause: The failed writer closed the temporary file writer, reopened the file read-only, and then requested a file synchronization operation through that read-only descriptor. That access mode is invalid for the required Windows flush, so durability failed before atomic replacement. The old path also lacked an explicit durable containing-directory synchronization result.
limitations: Directory synchronization is filesystem and API dependent; unsupported results are explicit and would prevent an unqualified success claim. This run reported synchronized directory handles for every counted write on both platforms.
Atomic replacement requires the temporary and destination files to share a containing directory and filesystem.
The qualification used fixed public strings and trivial shell exits. It did not perform a diagnostic search.
No physical power-loss injection was performed; ordering, synchronization calls, fresh-process reload, sealing, exact cardinality, and residue rejection were verified.
repair_strategy: Create the temporary file in the destination directory with an exclusive writable descriptor.
Write bytes, flush userspace buffers, and synchronize through the still-open writable descriptor.
Close the descriptor, atomically replace the destination, then synchronize the containing directory.
Record directory synchronization as synced or unsupported; never convert unsupported semantics into success.
Detect and reject interrupted atomic-write residue during read-only verification.
payload.scope: Synthetic collector infrastructure qualification only; no diagnostic workload was launched or replayed.
